title: The nests are manned before anyone looks: the first sites open on the beats' first tick, and a queued guard never waits
context: The owner, 2026-11-13: "I suspect we are spawning the enemies at the rocket sites/nests/cargo later rather than already being there. They appeared out of nowhere iirc." The landers of rocket-a, rocket-b and the wreck stand in the world from the first frame (src/content/base-layout.js, stage 1); their guards (55, 65 and 80 records) are queued by src/fx/expedition-glue.js openSite through storyApi.spawn and released by src/fx/enemy-step.js releaseSpawns. Branch r14-guards-present, probe first (--guards-present, a per-frame timeline of the guard records, the queue, the beats' phase and the shot).
outcome: Diagnosed: two causes, both 'records created late', not a pool, the crowd gate, a rise or a distance cull. (1) On the landing the nests were queued at the foundry's deploy (7.0 s, story-beats.js phase 'foundry'), under the arrivalTalk close-up; the enemy loop runs only while the world is not frozen (td-tab.js updateEnemies under !frozen), so all 200 waited in the queue and were put down in one frame at 11.8 s as the shot changed to arrivalHold. (2) A chapter start between the foundry and the study (?skip=dog at 'orders', ?skip=quiver, 'settled', 'construction') never crossed the foundry beat, and the late-start block opened the sites only for 'expedition': the nests came at the study beat, 55-80 bodies a site at once, the landers standing empty until then (test/story-beats.mjs pinned begun 0 at 'settled'). Also by reading: releaseSpawns stops at its first held or future entry, so a guard pushed behind a queued sector wave (a later site opens on a delivery, mid-sector) waited for the wave (test/enemy-step.mjs proves it on the fakes: red without the fix). Fixed: story-beats.js `manned` calls expeditionsBegin on the beats' first tick whatever the start (idempotent with the landing's and the expedition beat's calls); enemy-step.js releaseGuards puts every due guard down wherever it stands in the queue, and runs from releaseSpawns and from openSite (glue hook `settle`, wired through createExpeditionsHost), so a nest opened under a frozen close-up stands before the shot ends. No knob: the rule has no number. The guards stand idle on their site as before (guard-aggro.js), no blob, no rise (no breach source).
alternatives: Spawning the guards straight through spawnOne from the glue, bypassing the queue: rejected, the queue's Pearl room check (creatures.full) would be skipped; releaseGuards keeps it and only drops the line order for guards.

Populating nests by distance from every camera: not needed. The records already exist from the start on the expedition page (measured, the gunship sees 41 of 41); the Pearl kit culls by horizon and frustum per body (src/fx/cutis-maku/geometry.js update), so the bodies cost draw only in view. Frame time not measured.
Opening the sites at the first tick only for late starts: rejected, the landing itself put them down at 11.8 s in one frame under the arrival shots.
evidence: Before (probe on the landing, index.html?...&world=story): f1 t=0.06 s phase landed alive [0,0,0]; t=7.0 s phase dog-print shot arrivalTalk alive [0,0,0] queued guards 200 (head a guard); t=11.8 s alive [55,65,80] queued 0, one frame; t=12.0 s shot arrivalHold.

Before (an APFS clone of the base 1162ef92 with only the new suite dropped in): --guards-present on ?skip=dog red, alive [0,0,0] and no guard queued for 30 s, the beats from 'orders' into 'quiver-piloting' (t 21.1 s, takeControl); test/story-beats.mjs on the base asserts begun 0 for a 'settled' start.

After (c162034e): --guards-present PASS on the landing, ?skip=dog and ?skip=quiver: alive [55,65,80] at the harness's first frame on each (all nests up 0.1-0.2 s after the harness), no guard with a breach source or blob, Pearl bodies 54/55, 64/65, 79/80 (the small Reed's body is its own family's, not in the Pearl view), the hull 31-36 cells from the sites against an aggro reach of 10.8-13.2.

test/story-beats.mjs (every start phase mans the nests on its first tick; 'settled' once), test/enemy-step.mjs (three guards down on the first frame behind a wave due at 5 s; red with releaseGuards off), test/nest-guards.mjs (openSite settles once after the last guard). npm test 352 programs, npm run check, npm run architecture green; td-tab 5,365 lines, unchanged.

--nest-guards after: run 1 red at its chase step ('the rocket-b Reed is alive at the chase's start'; up and gunship green, the gunship drawing 65 of 65); run 2 green through the chase (Reed 1.71 -> 1.44 cells) and red only at blobs, as the base clone is (base chase Reed 1.00 -> 0.52 cells, red at blobs). The run-1 chase red is not reproduced; inferred flaky (the Reed starts 1.0-1.7 cells from the placed hull), not proven.
